subject: POC MAP: environment SLA runbook + credentials & peering next steps
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@healthlytics.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HealthLytics Procurement <procurement@healthlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: POC environment requirements and timing

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and infra asked me to consolidate the items we'll need to get the evaluation environment up and running so we can meet a mid-September pilot start. Key asks below:

- Org setup: invite 3 engineers and one admin; RBAC for read-only vs operator roles
- API keys: short-lived vs long-lived guidance; rotation policy for trial keys
- IP allowlist: static egress IPs for data plane calls (we'll provide CIDRs)
- VPC peering: schedule, expected downtime, and routing table changes
- SLA expectations for latency and availability during POC

Can you map these to a mutual action plan and a proposed cutover timeline? Procurement also asked for any certification evidence (SOC2) to include in the SOW.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Director, Platform Engineering
HealthLytics

Attachments: none
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@healthlytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-23T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: POC environment requirements and timing

Hi Samira —

Appreciate the clear list. I've sketched a short MAP and runbook draft that ties each dependency to an owner and date. High level timeline (proposal):

- Week 1 (Aug 24–28): org invites + RBAC mapping; we create the trial org and assign roles
- Week 2 (Aug 31–Sep 4): API keys provisioned; establish rotation cadence for trial (30d) and document controls
- Week 3 (Sep 7–11): IP allowlist verification and preflight tests from HealthLytics CIDRs
- Week 4 (Sep 14–18): VPC peering cutover (low-traffic window); final acceptance and SLA smoke tests

I attached a working runbook (map_runbook_v1.2.pdf) and a quick network sketch. A few notes:

- For the POC we recommend short-lived API keys (30 days) with an automated rotation webhook; we can issue long-lived tokens if procurement requires but will flag higher risk.
- VPC peering requires CIDR confirmation from your side; route propagation typically takes <15 minutes but we'll schedule an hour window for validation.
- We'll provide SOC2 summary and a link to the security questionnaire in the Drive link below.

Next steps: confirm the org invite list (names + emails) and the IP ranges. If that is ok, Ben will schedule the peering window and Marissa will own key issuance.

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: map_runbook_v1.2.pdf; network-peering-sketch.png
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-08-24T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: POC environment requirements and timing

Looping in operations notes for the peering cutover. Quick checklist for our runbook entry:

- Confirm HealthLytics CIDR blocks and any overlapping prefixes (deadline: Aug 28)
- Create peering request in cloud console and share request ID with HealthLytics
- Preflight: validate DNS resolution for our mappings (internal) and run synthetic latency checks (10m)
- Cutover window: Sep 14 02:00–03:00 PT (tentative) — low traffic; change control ticket will be opened
- Rollback plan: remove routes and revalidate application endpoints; expected rollback time <30m

Ben
Ben Carter
Cloud Ops Lead | Redwood Inference
